title: Ops latch controller for autonomous batching enactment
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: build an "ops latch" controller that mediates automated batching/caching recommendations from Optimize before they are applied to runtime fleets. The controller must provide a configurable staged rollout path (staging sims -> small canary -> expanded canary -> gradual ramp), operator approval hooks, and deterministic rollback triggers driven by telemetry. This ticket covers the backend controller, policy evaluation, canary runner integration, and the operator-facing webhook/escrow API. UI work (Console) will be tracked separately but integration points are described here.

Motivation: model- and workload-specific batching/cache tweaks materially reduce token cost but carry risk to latency and correctness. Previous incidents showed that fully automated commits without multi-stage verification caused regressions under tail-latency conditions. We need a runtime-side safety lane that can: (1) validate a proposed config against a simulated traffic profile, (2) run controlled traffic canaries with traffic shaping, (3) collect fidelity/latency/regression signals, (4) apply or rollback automatically based on thresholds or escalate to human operators.

Non-goals: console UI polish, billing-facing metering changes, large-scale autoscaler changes, or private-deployment-only features (we will support private later).

Design notes: the controller will be a stateless service with a small persistent store for rollout state and audit records. It will orchestrate three subsystems: SimRunner (local simulation using historical request traces), CanaryAgent (coordinates canary traffic routing and model variant selection), and VerdictEngine (policy evaluator that consumes telemetry and thresholds). The controller exposes: a REST API for Optimize to submit proposals, a webhook for operator escalation/acknowledgement, and an event stream of state transitions (Kafka topic). All changes are auditable and bound to a commit token that encodes the recommended config, provenance, and signature.

Security: proposals must be signed by Optimize service account; controller validates signatures and RBAC policies. KMS keys are used for storing minimal secrets; audit logs are forwarded to our central logging stack.

Acceptance criteria and success metrics are enumerated below.
acceptance_criteria: Controller accepts Optimize suggestion and creates a rollout object with immutable commit token
SimRunner can execute a simulation within the playground cluster and produce latency/cost delta summaries within 10 minutes for typical workloads
CanaryAgent can route 1-5% traffic to canary variant and expand to 25% under automatic policy
VerdictEngine triggers auto-rollback when any of: 99.9p latency increases > 30%, error rate increases > 0.5% absolute, or output-quality regression detected by provided eval set
Operator webhook/escrow API allows a human to approve or abort within the rollout timeline and stores acknowledgement in audit logs
End-to-end e2e tests exist for: simulate->canary->expand->rollback path with synthetic traffic
Telemetry emitted for each rollout step (created, sim_complete, canary_started, canary_metrics, decision_made) and is viewable on the Optimize rollout dashboard
implementation_plan: API contract: define /v1/rollouts create/get/ack endpoints and commit token schema (see design doc link)
Build SimRunner integration: mount archived traces, run deterministic simulator (node service) and output delta report
CanaryAgent integration with SmartRouter: implement traffic slice orchestration and fallback mappings
VerdictEngine policies: implement policy DSL for latency/errors/quality thresholds and escalation rules
Persistent state: small Postgres table for rollout states + encrypted blob storage for full commit payloads
Eventing: publish rollout lifecycle events to kafka.topic.optimize-rollouts for downstream console and alerting
CI: unit tests + integration harness that replays recorded traces and validates rollback triggers
Operational runbook: playbook for on-call with rollback commands and who-to-cc for escalations
telemetry: Emit metrics: rollout.duration_seconds, rollout.step (enum), canary.traffic_pct, canary.error_rate, canary.99p_latency_ms, sim.estimated_cost_delta
Log structured events with commit_token and correlation_id for traceability
Dashboard: create Optimize->Rollouts view with filters by model, customer, and commit author
Alerts: create SLO-based alert (page if 99.9p latency delta > 30% for any active rollout)
rollout_plan: 1) Submit proposal: Optimize POSTs suggestion to /v1/rollouts with commit payload
2) Sim stage: SimRunner runs offline simulation using 24h sample traces (fast-path) and returns cost/latency estimate within 10m
3) Passive canary: route 0.5% traffic for 30m to collect baseline vs canary metrics (no billing change yet)
4) Active canary: if sim metrics good, route 5% traffic for 1h with full billing impact
5) Expand/thermostat: auto-expand to 25% if metrics remain within thresholds, then to 100% in controlled ramp (48h total), or stop and rollback if thresholds breached
6) Operator escrow: if a rollout requests manual approval at any gate, pause and notify ops; store acknowledgement before proceeding
7) Finalize: mark rollout as succeeded, emit final report, and persist applied config to model-serving config store
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy DSL evaluation under synthetic metric streams
Integration tests that exercise end-to-end simulated traces -> canary routing -> verdict decision path
Chaos test: simulate noisy worker (slow kernels) during canary and ensure rollback triggers
Performance test: controller must handle 100 concurrent rollouts without >200ms median API latency
Security test: verify signature validation, RBAC enforcement, and audit trail retention
